name: Malattia Leventinese

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for Malattia Leventinese

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic drusen deposits in the macula on fundoscopic examination
Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance pattern
Identification of pathogenic EFEMP1 gene mutation (commonly R345W)
Progressive central vision loss documented by visual acuity testing
Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showing subretinal drusen deposits

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic macular drusen deposits plus either a positive family history or identification of EFEMP1 mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is confirmatory; clinical diagnosis can be made based on fundoscopic findings and family history.

pathognomonic.notes: Yellowish extracellular deposits in the macula visible on fundus exam
Gradual decline in visual acuity affecting central vision

common.notes: Visual distortion commonly reported by patients
Impaired color vision in affected individuals
Central blind spot in the visual field

occasional.notes: Reduced ability to see in low light conditions

rare.notes: Abnormal blood vessel growth under the retina
Degeneration of retinal pigment epithelium cells
Elevated intraocular pressure as a complication

imaging: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showing subretinal deposits
Fluorescein angiography demonstrating drusen and possible neovascularization
genetic: Pathogenic EFEMP1 gene mutation (commonly R345W variant)
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Multifactorial etiology with environmental risk factors
Presence of vitelliform lesions rather than drusen
Mutations in BEST1 or PRPH2 genes

redFlags: Rapid progression of central vision loss
Sudden onset of metamorphopsia or scotomas
references: Stone EM et al. Identification of a gene that causes dominant drusen. N Engl J Med. 1999.
Seddon JM et al. Macular dystrophies: clinical features and molecular genetics. Eye (Lond). 2013.
